review.reason: Multiple runtime-owned comment attachments are unreachable from package rules (FINDINGS 9): the mid-union block comment becomes a suffix that forces its group, the opening-bracket comment stays a suffix of `[`, and type-parameter and type-argument comments attach on the opposite side from Prettier. `Piped` also needs a declared leading `|` emitted only in the broken branch, an opcode the IR still lacks. The alias semicolon cannot simply be pulled onto the last union line: removing that `soft` was tested and made this case non-idempotent after the trailing union comment reattached.

The @80 attachment limits remain (FINDINGS 9), plus the broken union needs a leading break-only `|` that no opcode emits and the suffix comment participates in fit where Prettier ignores it (FINDINGS 6). The tested package-level semicolon tightening made comments@80 non-idempotent, so it is not an equivalent repair.

Python-style two-group arguments could reproduce Prettier last-object hugging, so this is not inability and not a package bug. TypeScript and JavaScript use byte-identical `list` and `arguments` rules; the JavaScript corpus has no multi-argument call ending in an object, so it never exposed the same mismatch. Keep the cross-language rule that every item in a broken list gets its own line instead of adding a TypeScript-only last-object special case.

The call chain is a left-nested alternating `member_expression` / `call_expression` spine. Existing `flatten` handles homogeneous same-kind spines only, so breaking at every dot needs the heterogeneous-chain capability in FINDINGS 11. The constructor hunk is separately expressible by special-casing TypeScript parameter properties, but the shared JavaScript/TypeScript formal-parameter rule is the more consistent house layout and avoids a one-file rule.

This file combines established limits: the alternating call/member spine needs heterogeneous flatten (FINDINGS 11); Prettier selects assignment, generic, and nested-ternary candidates that independent Wadler groups cannot rank (FINDINGS 15); broken unions need an inserted leading `|`; and enclosing collection content remains on the fit stack while inner generic/object groups decide. The class-brace and one-argument call differences are expressible special cases, but keeping shared JavaScript list/class rules is the cross-language house choice; those do not remove the file-level design limits.

Prettier hangs the alias before laying out the conditional; this package groups the ternary itself. The builder experiment is decisive: moving the group to the alias matches `Unpacked` and misses `DeepPartial` in the same file, so one fixed group layout cannot choose the two candidates Prettier chooses (FINDINGS 15).

The assignment-versus-conditional conflict from @80 remains (FINDINGS 15). At 40 the independently fitting type-parameter, type-argument, mapped-body, and ternary groups also choose different break sites from Prettier; moving the outer group trades the `Unpacked` and `DeepPartial` hunks rather than resolving both, so this needs candidate-layout selection rather than another fixed package rule.

While `Array<{ list: number[] }>` is measured, the enclosing array/type docs remain on the printer stack, so the generic group is judged not to fit; Prettier instead hangs the value and keeps the generic flat. Removing or moving the group changes the surrounding array/object cases. The missing capability is a layout candidate that can fit the inner generic independently of the enclosing collection, not a node-kind refusal.

`drop` now reaches both parens: `(` and `)` are declared punctuation and neither carries a comment, so both refusal guards pass and the redundant pair disappears. But applying that rule to `parenthesized_expression` also deletes required control-flow parens (`if (x)` and `if (n === 0)` became invalid `if x` forms). Rules cannot select the deletion by parent position (FINDINGS 10). The same file also needs unconditional ASI semicolon insertion, for which no sanctioned token-addition policy exists.

Same verified result as @80: `drop` removes the redundant pair but its two guards cannot distinguish redundancy, and a global parenthesized-expression rule deletes required `if` parens. Parent-position-sensitive dispatch (FINDINGS 10) is still missing, as is unconditional semicolon insertion. The report claim about an additional generic-call hunk was stale; the current exact diff has only paren deletion and semicolon insertion.

Both layouts fit only by choosing a different break site: Prettier breaks `load(` parameters and keeps `Promise<string>` flat, while the independent parameter and return-type groups keep the parameter flat and break the generic. No package predicate sees or ranks those two candidate layouts; this is FINDINGS 15, not a fixable call-rule omission.

The old JavaScript fill/comment coupling is stale: current `fill` preserves BreakParent comments, and this number array has no comments. `fill` was applied and fixes @80. At 40 it packs through `170` because each fill choice does not reserve the break-only comma that `trail` adds afterward, producing a 41-column second line; omitting `trail` loses Prettier trailing commas and reverting to `each` loses @80. The missing capability is tail-aware fill/trailing-separator measurement (the FINDINGS 8/21 boundary).

The broken template union needs a declared leading `|` emitted only in the broken branch; neither `trail`, `drop`, nor the new unconditional-paren mode can insert an arbitrary leading token conditionally. The flat literal union also exposes the fixed alias-versus-union grouping choice and its break-only semicolon gap. Tightening that gap globally was tested and broke comment-union idempotence, so it is not an equivalent package edit.

Broken unions need an inserted leading `|`, but the IR exposes no break-conditional leading-token opcode; the new `paren true` mode is balanced-paren-specific and does not generalise. The nested conditional stays flat because an inner group cannot inherit or rank the broken outer candidate (FINDINGS 2/15). Pulling the semicolon onto the last line globally was tested and broke comments@80 idempotence.

The missing break-conditional leading `|` affects the top-level, generic, constraint, and function unions. The intersection and nested conditional choose different break candidates at 40 than at 80, which one fixed package grouping cannot reproduce (FINDINGS 15, with ancestor-break context from FINDINGS 2). The semicolon tightening workaround was disproved by an idempotence failure in comments@80.
